summary: Pattern is a sophisticated computational tool I developed to modernize the interpretation of protein gel electrophoresis by integrating key experimental variables such as molecular weight, electric voltage, gel length, and run time to generate a precise simulation of where protein bands should appear. Users can overlay these digital predictions onto photographs of actual experimental results, enabling confident verification of protein identities and reducing ambiguity in gel analysis. In an expanded application, an astronaut aboard the International Space Station could upload an amino acid sequence and use Pattern to predict the corresponding gel pattern, allowing direct comparison with experimental data to identify an exact protein in the unique microgravity environment of the station. By combining computational modeling with real-world gel images, Pattern supports more reliable protein identification, improves experimental interpretation, and extends the utility of electrophoresis analysis to remote and resource-constrained settings such as space-based research. This approach transforms gel electrophoresis from a primarily visual and interpretive technique into a more precise, verifiable, and accessible analytical workflow for both terrestrial laboratories and orbital scientific investigations.
